summary: Mount Hood NF lookout in Clackamas County, OR: 14-ft L-4 tower dated 1933 (or 1934), deactivated 1964 and gone by 1965; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Tower gone by 1965; no source we read describes what remains at the site
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Mount Hood National Forest

events.note: 14-foot L-4 tower per the register and firelookout.com; Forest Lookouts dates it 1934
Tower legs replaced; the tower has nine leg supports
Inspection found rotting beams and a sagging floor and recommended replacement
Registered September 21, 2010; nominated by Ray Kresek

evidence.supports: built 1933 as a 14-foot L-4 tower; gone by 1965
evidence.quote: In 1933, the USFS built a 14' L-4 tower, which was gone by 1965.
This lookout was built in 1934, the tower is rotting, rickety and should be replaced.

evidence.supports: about 35 miles southwest of Mount Hood

evidence.quote: The tower legs on Thunder Mountain Lookout were replaced
The floor is sagging and rotting out
This structure is also used by the public.

notes_for_editor: Built year disputed: 1933 (register, firelookout.com) vs 1934 (Forest Lookouts and its 1963 inspection quote). Record design was null; filled from the register and firelookout.com. The Forest Lookouts page includes a 1963 inspection line giving the total height as 5 ft, which does not fit a 14-ft tower; not used. A different Thunder Mountain lookout in Pend Oreille County, Washington (willhiteweb.com) came up in search and must not be mixed in. No access or condition information for today was found.
